beats.text: The United States spends 16.7% of its economy on health. Bangladesh spends just 2.2%.
That puts the American system at the very top of global spending.
The United States spends 5.1 times as much as India, where health receives 3.3%.
Major European economies spend heavy too: Germany sits at 12.3%, Austria at 11.8%, France at 11.5%, and the UK at 11.1%.
Yet in Nigeria, current health spending accounts for 4.2% of GDP.
This counts medical goods and services consumed, excluding capital costs like hospitals or emergency vaccine stocks.
How much of its wealth should a nation dedicate to health?
